rationale: The six objectives (O1-O6) are clear, measurable and pertinent, each citing specific EO/SR codes, but the only ledger entries are a TRL inference and a single aggregate 'objective_topic_mapping' claim whose status=confirmed carries an empty source_ref, not a real one; the extensive 'Beyond the state of the art' claims in ¶10-11 (protocols published, crosswalks, provenance-tracked pipeline as an advance over discarded project-internal reconciliation) have no corresponding claim-ledger entry at all, so the state-of-the-art assertion rests on no confirmed, sourced claim.

The six objectives (O1–O6) are clear, measurable and pertinent, each tied to a named expected outcome/scope requirement, but the only claim-ledger entries are objective_topic_mapping (status=confirmed yet source_ref is blank, so no real source) and no_trl_target (status=inferred, no source_ref); the entire 'Beyond the state of the art' paragraph (¶10–11), which carries the SOTA advance claim, has no corresponding claim-ledger entry at all, so the load-bearing SOTA assertion rests on no confirmed claim with a real source_ref.

The six objectives (O1–O6) are clear, measurable and pertinent, each tied to named EO/SR codes, and the 'Beyond the state of the art' spans state a specific advance (publishing reconciliation as protocols/crosswalks/pipeline vs. current practice discarding it) rather than generic ambition — so addressal is strong. But grounding fails: the ledger supplies only two entries, one 'inferred' (no_trl_target#33) and one 'confirmed' but with an empty source_ref (objective_topic_mapping#34), so no load-bearing claim — including the central beyond-SOTA assertion and the KPI/target/duration/budget figures in ¶8–9 — rests on a confirmed claim with a real source_ref.

B.1.2¶0-4 give a concrete methodology (named multisensory integration architecture, three stated assumptions, staged delivery logic, five named challenges with mitigations) grounded in confirmed claims (#22, #31, #32, #46); interdisciplinarity (¶7), gender dimension (¶9, backed by confirmed #19 though the substantive disaggregation claim #20 is only 'inferred'), open science practices (¶10, backed by confirmed #37, naming EOSC/Common Data Spaces/GBIF/OBIS/LUCAS/provenance pipelines) and the DMP deliverable (¶11, backed by confirmed #16) are all explicitly treated rather than silent, though every ledger entry shown carries an empty source_ref, weakening the grounding somewhat.

The section substantively addresses methodology (B.1.2¶0-4: integration architecture, three named assumptions, staged delivery), interdisciplinarity (¶7-8, naming six disciplines plus SSH), gender dimension (¶9, explicit human-facing disaggregation), open science (¶10, FAIR/EOSC/GBIF-OBIS-LUCAS), and names the DMP as a distinct six-month deliverable (¶11) — but every claim-ledger entry backing these load-bearing statements (e.g. methodology_observation_chain#32, integration_architecture_model#22, methodology_assumptions#31, dmp_distinct_deliverable_fair#16, gender_requirement_recorded#19, open_science_fair_core#37) carries status=confirmed yet an empty source_ref, so none is actually grounded to a real source despite the confirmed label.

Methodology (B.1.2¶0-4: integration architecture, assumptions, staged delivery), gender dimension (¶9), and open science (¶10, DMP ¶11) are each explicitly addressed and backed by confirmed claim-ledger entries (integration_architecture_model, methodology_assumptions, methodology_observation_chain, gender_requirement_recorded, open_science_fair_core, dmp_distinct_deliverable_fair), but the interdisciplinary-approach span (¶7, listing molecular biology, ecology, earth observation, AI, policy analysis) has no corresponding claim-ledger entry at all, and every ledger entry in the pack carries an empty source_ref even where status=confirmed, so grounding for a required element is missing and grounding generally is unverifiable against a real source.

Spans B.2.1(a)/(b) and B.2.3 tie specific project results (D6.2/D6.3 uncertainty-bearing classification, D2.2 architecture, D6.1 split-protocol resource) to named topic outcomes EO-01–03 and then to all six destination impacts EI-01–06, with specific target groups (research groups, standards bodies, competent authorities under named directives, farmers via P05's network) and out-of-scope barriers (standards adoption, typology drift, regulatory change, user-network dependency, eDNA reference gaps) each paired with a mitigation; the valuation-clause gap is honestly flagged as only partly addressed rather than overclaimed. Grounding is largely solid via confirmed claim-ledger entries (outcomes_oc1_to_oc7, destination_expected_impacts_six, target_groups, pathway_maps_outcome_then_impact) and the honestly-flagged assumed entries for the valuation gap, though every ledger entry carries an empty source_ref, which weakens but does not negate traceability since the prose itself anchors each claim to a specific deliverable code.

B.2.1¶4 and ¶8 trace each of the three topic outcomes and all six destination impacts to a specific project deliverable/mechanism (e.g., D6.2/D6.3 uncertainty-bearing trend maps for EO-01; D3.1-D3.4/D6.2 FAIR release for EI-02; D7.1/D7.2/D7.3 for EI-05), target groups are named specifically (¶13) and matched to named barriers with mitigations beyond project scope (¶18-20, e.g. standards adoption via D3.4 disposition tracking, typology drift via versioned D3.2), and the claim ledger confirms outcomes_oc1_to_oc7, destination_expected_impacts_six, pathway_maps_outcome_then_impact and target_groups as status=confirmed while the valuation gap is honestly flagged as assumed/partial rather than overclaimed. The one weakness is that every ledger entry, including confirmed ones, carries an empty source_ref, so full source traceability cannot be independently verified from this pack alone.

B.2.1¶4-¶8 and the B.2.3 canvas map specific project results (D2.2, D5.3, D6.1-D6.3, D3.1-D3.4, D7.1-D7.3) to the topic's three named outcomes and the destination's six named impacts (EI-01 to EI-06), with named target groups (¶13, data-infrastructure operators, competent authorities under named directives, farmers/land managers, etc.) and explicit out-of-scope barriers with mitigations in (b); ledger claims outcomes_oc1_to_oc7, destination_expected_impacts_six, pathway_maps_outcome_then_impact and target_groups are status=confirmed and the valuation gap is honestly flagged as assumed/partial rather than overclaimed, though none of the cited claim entries carry a populated source_ref, which weakens strict traceability verification.

Span B.2.2¶4 pairs each measure (FAIR release, standards submission, reporting-shaped outputs, farm-tool indicators, global-facility publication, plain-language messaging) with its target group and an explicit suitability justification, and IP strategy (¶20-23: copyright/open licences, patents excluded, SME trade secret carve-out) plus post-project follow-up (¶28-29) are both addressed; these measures are backed by confirmed claim-ledger entries (dissemination_fair_release#20, standardisation_submission#46, indicators_into_farm_management_tools#26, target_groups#48, wp7_carries_measures#54), with partner-dependent measures (P05/P06/P10) honestly flagged as assumed rather than overclaimed, so the expectation is substantively addressed and grounded despite the ledger's uniformly blank source_ref field.

B.2.2¶4 gives a per-target-group measure with a suitability justification in each cell, ¶20-23 outlines an IP strategy (open-source/FAIR foreground, patents excluded, SME trade-secret background), and ¶28-29 addresses post-project continuation — all backed by confirmed ledger entries (dissemination_fair_release, standardisation_submission, indicators_into_farm_management_tools, wp7_carries_measures, ria_not_ia). The section also honestly flags non-grounded elements (P04/P05/P06/P10 participation 'assumed', financial-actor pathway not claimed) rather than overclaiming, though none of the ledger entries carry a populated source_ref, leaving traceability to source documents unverifiable from the pack alone.

B.2.2 gives a six-row target-group/measure/justification table plus dissemination, exploitation, standardisation, communication, follow-up and IP-strategy subsections, each tied to a target group and a deliverable; the load-bearing mechanism claims (fair_release, indicators_into_farm_management_tools, standardisation_submission, wp7_carries_measures, target_groups) are all status=confirmed in the ledger. The section is weakened by every confirmed claim lacking a source_ref and by several measures (P05/P06/P10/P04 participation) being explicitly flagged as assumed rather than confirmed, so grounding is present but not fully robust.

The section lays out seven WPs, tasks, deliverables, a deliverable Gantt, milestones with verification criteria, and a risk register with likelihood/severity/mitigation (B.3.1¶30-32), but effort per work package is categorically absent — Table 3.1a and 3.1f mark every person-month 'not agreed'/'TBD' (claim implementation_section.effort_shares#26, status=assumed, source_ref empty) and the overall resources are not justified, only deferred to a future lump-sum budget response (budget_lump_sum_external#13, source_ref empty); the risk register itself is explicitly flagged assumed with no confirmed source (critical_risks_assumed#21). The rubric requires effort assigned per WP with resources justified and load-bearing figures grounded in confirmed, sourced entries — none of the effort or risk claims meet status=confirmed with a real source_ref, so the expectation is addressed in structure but not grounded, and the missing effort figures alone are disqualifying per the rubric.

The section delivers a full WP/task/deliverable/milestone structure and a risk register (R01-R13) with likelihood, severity and mitigation (span B.3.1¶32), but Table 3.1f and 3.1a show person-months as entirely 'TBD'/'not agreed' and the claim ledger confirms this (effort_shares#26, status=assumed, 'not agreed; workpackage_seed.json carries no person-months'), so effort per work package and the overall resources are never assigned or justified with a figure — the rubric's explicit disqualifier ('A work plan with no effort figures... must not pass') applies, and the risk assessment itself is only status=assumed with no source_ref.

The work-package structure, tasks, deliverables, milestones with means of verification, and a risk register (R01-R13) with likelihood/severity/mitigation are present, but effort is nowhere assigned: Table 3.1a/3.1f show 'not agreed'/TBD for every WP and partner (span B.3.1¶13, ¶34-35), matching claim effort_shares#26 (status=assumed, 'not agreed; workpackage_seed.json carries no person-months'), and the rubric is explicit that a work plan with no effort figures must not pass. The critical-risk assessment itself is only status=assumed (critical_risks_assumed#21), so even the risk/mitigation component lacks confirmed grounding.

Roles, disciplines, infrastructure access and complementarity are described in detail (B.3.2¶5, ¶12, ¶16-18), but the load-bearing capability claim behind every participant is 'participation' itself, and all twelve partner_participation ledger entries are status=assumed with no source_ref, a fact the prose itself repeatedly concedes ('Every partner's participation is an operator assumption', B.3.2¶2, ¶13, ¶30); only two unrelated facts (composition rule, gender-gap) are confirmed, so the consortium capacity/role narrative is addressed but not grounded.

B.3.2 extensively addresses role/capacity (disciplinary table ¶5, management roles ¶20, infrastructure access ¶12-13, complementarity chains ¶16-18), but every partner_participation claim (#0-#11) is status=assumed with no source_ref, and the prose itself concedes this ('Every partner's participation is an operator assumption', ¶2; 'Access to all of this is assumed, because no partner's participation is confirmed', ¶13), so the load-bearing capacity/role claims are not grounded in confirmed ledger entries.

The section substantively addresses roles, disciplines, complementarity and infrastructure access (B.3.2¶5,¶12-¶13,¶16-¶20), but every one of the twelve partner participation entries in the claim ledger is status=assumed with no source_ref, and the prose itself concedes 'every partner's participation is an operator assumption' (¶2) and 'access to all of this is assumed' (¶13), so the load-bearing capacity/role claims are not grounded in confirmed ledger entries.
